mappings.note: Defines democracy and separates the direct from the representative form. CG-SST3 is the goal about the working of Indian democracy; its outcomes cover the role and levels of government, not the concept of democracy itself.
The three organs and what each does - the make-up of government, which LO-219 covers ('especially' at the local level, not exclusively). Not LO-220, since no tier is being distinguished.
Why three tiers are needed: the item is precisely about identifying local, state and union levels and what each is for, which is LO-220.
The COVID lockdown project asks WHICH TIERS acted (LO-220) and what each ORGAN did (LO-219). Both halves are set out in the stem.
Why rules are needed when many people live together - the ordering function that government exists to perform, so LO-219. Not CG-SST3, since no democratic value or process is at issue.
Defines governance as deciding, organising and enforcing; the core vocabulary of the government's role.
Defines government as the body that makes and enforces rules - the companion definition to governance, under LO-219.
That laws can be reviewed and changed over time; a property of how government works, so LO-219.
Names the more important societal rules 'laws' - again the vocabulary of governance, hence LO-219.
New cybercrime laws as the government responding to technological change; the law-making role of government, so LO-219.
Places the local government at town and village level - a tier-identification item, squarely LO-220.
Judicial review as part of checks and balances: the judiciary's role in government (LO-219) and a constitutional safeguard (CG-SST3).
Direct against representative democracy by how citizens take part - a question about the form of democracy, so the goal rather than a government-structure outcome.
A citizen approaching the judiciary over a law that infringes fundamental rights: a constitutional value (CG-SST3) enforced through an organ of government (LO-219).
Grassroots democracy empowering ordinary citizens locally - the chapter's title idea; CG-SST3 names democratic processes at the local level and LO-219 the government's role there.
Parliament as the national law-making assembly; identifying the union tier's legislature, so LO-220.
Finds the level of government wrongly matched to its jurisdiction across central, state and local - a tier-identification item, hence LO-220.
The President as nominal head of the Central Government and Supreme Commander - an office of the union tier, so LO-220.
National defence as a central rather than state responsibility; a division-of-powers item between tiers, so LO-220.
The Vidhan Sabha as the state legislature - identifying an institution of the state tier, hence LO-220.
The Governor as nominal head at state level; the state-tier counterpart of the President item, so LO-220.
Police and law and order as state subjects - again the division of functions between tiers, so LO-220.

Dr Kalam's 'Missile Man' name earned by his work on India's missile programme: India's contribution in science, which LO-224 covers. Not LO-220, because the question is about his scientific career, not the presidency as an office.
Why every citizen cannot rule directly in a large country - the argument for representative democracy, so the goal.
Matches responsibilities to tiers and settles on village sanitation with the local government: tier identification (LO-220) and the work a rural local body actually does (LO-221).
Where a citizen goes when a government action violates a fundamental right: a constitutional guarantee (CG-SST3) served by the judiciary (LO-219).
India as the largest functioning democracy because it holds regular elections under adult franchise - the working of Indian democracy, which is CG-SST3.
Finds Vidhan Sabha wrongly called a national body among Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha and MLA; the item turns on which tier each institution belongs to, so LO-220.
Locates the debate and vote on a national law in Parliament - identifying the union legislature, hence LO-220.
Separation of powers among the three organs; a point about how government is built, so LO-219 rather than a tier outcome.
Adult citizens' right to choose their government and why large populations need representation - the working of Indian democracy, so CG-SST3.
Rejects 'electing the President' as a judicial function among law-making, implementing and interpreting; an organ-to-function item, so LO-219.
Statement set separating the Governor from the Chief Minister and the High Court from the legislature: organs (LO-219) within the state tier (LO-220).
A highway project running through Assembly budget, PWD execution and High Court dispute: all three organs (LO-219) at the state level (LO-220).
MLAs as members of the state assemblies - naming the representatives of the state tier, so LO-220.
MPs as members of the Lok Sabha; the union-tier counterpart of the MLA item, hence LO-220.
India's roughly 970 million voters in 2024 - the scale of the electorate, which is about the working of Indian democracy, so CG-SST3.
Eighteen as the voting age under universal adult suffrage - a constitutional provision governing the democratic process, hence CG-SST3.
